subject: Post-demo: quantization tradeoffs & eval next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver King <oliver.king@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-29T17:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: quantization tradeoffs & eval next steps

Hi Oliver — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed (copied Lauren for visibility):

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: productionize summarization + guided Q&A over internal docs; target latency <= 300ms p50 and <1s p95 for 2k context windows.
- Throughput requirement: ~40 concurrent sessions at peak.
- Quality sensitivity: summaries must preserve entity accuracy; we care more about precision than brevity.

What I recommend we run next (short term):
1) Model fit + eval run: baseline on Llama-2 70B, Llama-3 70B, and Red-optimized 40B (we talked about cost/latency tradeoffs).
2) Quantization trade study: AWQ (4-bit), GPTQ (4-bit), and FP8 experimental path for 40B/70B variants to measure throughput vs quality regression.
3) Prompt set: we will use the sample prompt set you shared plus an internal 50-case entity-preservation eval. Attachments include the trade-study PDF and the prompt set sample.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Confirm the sample prompts in the attached acme_benchmark-sample-prompts.json are the right distribution.
- Are there any regulatory constraints on model residency (need VPC/on-prem)?

Next steps / timeline:
- We can schedule a 2-hour POC kickoff next week to run the model-fit/eval and capture token-latency traces (need a technical attendee).
- Deliverable: a short report with per-model quality deltas, throughput numbers, and recommendation (target: 3 options: high-quality, balanced, low-cost).

Attachments: redwood_awq-gptq-fp8-trade-study-20260729.pdf, acme_benchmark-sample-prompts.json

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Dev to provision the POC infra once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Oliver — happy to lead the POC. A few technical notes and proposal for the kickoff agenda: 

Technical clarifications:
- Residency: we can run the POC in Acme's VPC using Redwood Private; alternatively, our hosted EU region can be used if you only need data residency for logs/telemetry (we will ensure EU region endpoints and no cross-region replication). If you want customer-managed KMS, Private is the path.
- POC infra: I’ll provision two rows: 1x 70B (A100/80GB) and 1x 40B (H100/80GB) with quantized variants. We’ll test AWQ (4-bit per-tensor), GPTQ (4-bit per-channel), and a limited FP8 baseline.
- Eval metrics: ROUGE/ROUGE-L for summarization plus an entity-F1 (we'll run a lightweight exact-match for named entities). We’ll also record p50/p95 generation latency and tokens/sec throughput under the 40 concurrent session load using the Redwood bench tool.

Suggested kickoff agenda (2 hours):
- 00:00-00:15: Introductions & success criteria (Marissa + Oliver)
- 00:15-00:45: Prompt set walk-through and finalize the 50-case entity-preservation list (Oliver)
- 00:45-01:30: Run baseline inference runs (Llama-3 70B, Red-40B) with FP16, then AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 variants; collect logs
- 01:30-02:00: Review preliminary quality vs throughput deltas and define follow-ups

Commands I’ll run (example):
- redwood bench run --model llama-3-70b --quant none --prompts acme_benchmark-sample-prompts.json --concurrency 40 --context 2048 --out results/70b-fp16.json
- redwood bench run --model red-40b --quant awq4 --prompts acme_benchmark-sample-prompts.json --concurrency 40 --context 2048 --out results/40b-awq.json

If that looks good I’ll provision infra on Aug 2 and send a calendar invite for Aug 3 09:00 PST.

Thanks,
Dev Patel

All — attaching the 10 high-ambiguity prompts inline here for convenience and confirming the kickoff. Also, procurement has requested a short statement of work (POC SOW) and an invoice for the reserved infra time (estimate: 3 days). They asked for the SOW to include: scope (models tested), metrics captured (ROUGE, entity-F1, latency), and the ownership of artifacts (we retain the prompts and redwood provides the results CSV).

High-ambiguity prompts (10):

2) "I have a flight tomorrow but haven't got a confirmation — did you get my booking?"
3) "The product shows a different address than mine, is that an error?"
4) "Why did my order change status to canceled? I didn't cancel it."
5) "I tried resetting my password but never got the email."
6) "This policy sounds different than what my rep told me — which is correct?"
7) "I got an error code 502 while uploading files — what does that mean?"
8) "Can you help me merge two accounts? I'm worried about duplicates."
9) "My subscription auto-renewed but I thought it was canceled."
10) "The summary you gave me seems to drop a critical customer name — can you re-check?"

Oliver — procurement will follow up on the SOW/invoice. See you Aug 3 09:00 PST.
